rule_paths.reason: Golden vectors, devnet transcripts and documentation: public test keys (anvil account 0, 0x01.. dev keys) and public member keys, not secrets (checked 2026-10-23; gitleaks agrees, .gitleaks.toml). A secret anywhere else is still reported.
Test code: a panic is a test failure, which is the intent.
Tests create scratch directories under the OS temp dir for throwaway stores and sandboxes; the daemon's store path comes from its config.
near-admin is a devnet set-up helper run by the operator (devnet/hawkeye-devnet); its argv is the operator's own command line, not a trust boundary.
Local solc-js shim invoked by forge with forge's own --base-path/--include-path arguments on the developer's machine; reading those paths is its job. Never runs in CI or production.

The devnet harness starts and drives local regtest nodes, anvil and Hawkeye processes and talks to them over 127.0.0.1 HTTP by design; argv comes from its own constants and the operator's own command line (`hawkeye-devnet cli ...` execs ycash-cli with the operator's arguments). Never shipped, never run on a public network.

contrib/secops/code-scanning-triage.py runs `gh api` with an argv list (no shell) built from constants, the alert number from the API and the workflow-supplied repository name; it runs only in .github/workflows/code-scanning.yml with that job's own token. A subprocess call anywhere else is still reported.
